name: Code Scan
tagline: Static security review of code you own. Forked agents read every candidate file, and each finding is disproved or reported at file:line.
who: Teams with a large codebase no security reviewer has read: engineers and founders who want their own repo audited for exploitable bugs. You own the code, so nothing leaves your workspace and no live host is touched.
how:
Your agent reads the code in depth rather than pattern-matching it:

- A fast pattern scan covers the whole repo for free and flags the files worth a closer look.
- Dozens of cheap forked sub-agents then work across those files, one batch each, reading for auth bypasses, injection, SSRF, path traversal, hardcoded secrets and logic flaws.
- The review is static. It never runs or exploits the code.
- Every candidate finding is then attacked: an independent pass tries to disprove it and checks git history for a fix that already landed. Only what survives is reported.

You get a written report and a findings sheet. Each finding carries the file:line, the code, the impact and a concrete fix. Both go to you and no one else.
